claims.text: The book Design Patterns (known as the GoF / "Gang of Four" book) catalogues many design patterns for object-oriented software; the lesson gives no count.
claims.source_hint: Design Patterns: Elements of Reusable Object-Oriented Software (catalogue of patterns)

claims.text: Strategy pattern: each variant of a rule is its own class behind a shared type; the class that needs it (the context, here CheckoutTotal) is handed one of those objects (a strategy) instead of branching itself.
claims.source_hint: glossary strategy-pattern; GoF book, Strategy pattern

claims.text: At stage-2 CheckoutTotal is a sealed class with primary-constructor parameter ShippingFee shippingFee; ForItems sums Quantity * UnitPriceVnd and returns that total plus shippingFee.ForOrder(itemsTotalVnd). It has no if/switch on kind and no new of a fee class.
In C#, a class's primary-constructor parameters (the list after the class name) must be supplied when creating an instance, so every new CheckoutTotal(...) has to pass a ShippingFee argument.
Calling the abstract ForOrder through a ShippingFee-typed parameter runs the override of the object's actual type (StandardShipping, ExpressShipping, ...), chosen at run time.
claims.source_hint: C# language reference: abstract/override, virtual method dispatch

claims.text: CheckoutTotalTests uses items (1 x 1,250,000) and (2 x 450,000) = 2,150,000 VND; with StandardShipping the expected total is 2,150,000 (free from 2,000,000), with ExpressShipping 2,210,000 (fee 60,000).
At stage-2 the only code creating a CheckoutTotal is CheckoutTotalTests in SamplesTests.cs, each test passing a concrete kind created with new.
Samples/Oop/ShippingFee.cs (abstract ShippingFee with StandardShipping, ExpressShipping, PickUpInStore) is identical at stage-0 and stage-2; CheckoutTotal.cs does not exist before stage-2.

claims.text: Strategy differs from plain polymorphism: polymorphism is the language feature; Strategy is the design decision to make one rule replaceable by handing the object in from outside (here via constructor injection).
Strategy is worth its extra types only when the rule really varies; for one variant with no plan for more, a single method is easier to follow.
With Strategy the branching disappears from the code that uses the rule; the remaining choice of which object to create is made once where the object is built.
